newsitem.title: USA: Equisure denies stock exchange charges.
newsitem.headline: Equisure denies stock exchange charges.

text.p: Equisure Inc said Friday it rejected "patently absurd" allegations made by the American Stock Exchange, which has said it began formal proceedings that could eventually lead to the delisting of the stock.

Equisure said it received a letter on Friday from the exchange that alleges, among other things, significant insider trading by principals and affiliates of the company. In a statement, Equisure said the exchange also "insinuated in its letter that the company has virtually no money, no business and no offices except for a one-man executive suite in Minnesota."

"Until AMEX suspended shares of the company, business was fine," Barry Harding, a director of Equisure, said in a statement. "Truthfully though, I cannot say that the damage to our reputation and credibility as a result of the exchange's actions is not generating concern among the insurance clients of the company."

Equisure said its directors "confirm unequivocally" that none of them have been involved in any illegal insider trading activity. The company also said its financial advisors confirmed that Equisure's investment position had not materially changed since March 31, 1997.
Equisure said it has offices Monaco and Belgium in addition to 2,000 square feet of newly leased office space in Minneapolis.
Equisure, a reinsurance company, said it is considering its legal position with respect to actions taken by the exchange.

Earlier, the American Stock Exchange said it initiated formal proceedings to review the continued listing eligibility of Equisure. The exchange declined to comment on specific reasons for the Equisure review.
